runs.content: Monday's rotation deep-dives Finance + Crypto. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-20), Crypto had no new material (last refresh was 09-19), but Finance had a 15-clipping clippings-sorter batch today, which supplied both connections. First: finance/short-research/source-morningstar-uk-most-shorted-2026-09-18.md flags Ceres Power (CWR, LSE) at 13.29% net short interest — a UK-listed solid-oxide fuel cell (SOFC) company marketed as a 'clean-energy/data-centre power solution' but hit with sell downgrades and a Grizzly Research bear report questioning partnership profitability, against a widening operating loss. finance/ideas/idea-bloom-energy.md's own Competitive Landscape table lists Plug Power (PEM) and FuelCell Energy (MCFC) as Bloom's competitors but omits Ceres — despite Ceres running Bloom's own core SOFC technology, making it the closer technology peer. More importantly, Ceres is a live market test of exactly the 'barely profitable, priced for perfect execution' Bear Case idea-bloom-energy.md already raises about Bloom itself — short-sellers are actively betting against the same AI-power narrative one ticker over, and neither page (nor ai-tech/model-dc-power-regional-balance-2026-06-25.md, which calls on-site fuel cells an unqualified 'immediate — already happening' winner) cites the others. Second: finance/source-guardian-ai-slowdown-bubble-2026-09-20.md names concrete, dated margin evidence — OpenAI 'repeatedly cutting fees to retain customers,' Anthropic's 'adjusted operating income' positive 'only by excluding many real costs' — for exactly the risk ai-tech/data-token-generation-pricing-gpu-comparison-2026-08-05.md already names once, in the abstract, as 'massive margin compression risk if open-weight models close the quality gap,' but elsewhere frames token deflation mainly as a benign scaling story. Neither page grounds the abstract risk in a named company until today's Guardian piece. Concrete next steps: add a Ceres Power row to idea-bloom-energy.md's Competitive Landscape table cross-linked to the short-interest screen; add the OpenAI/Anthropic margin evidence to the AI & Tech token-pricing page's margin-compression Key Insight. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-20.

Sunday's rotation picks whichever domain has gone longest without a deep-dive — Work qualified (only 2 pages, unchanged since 2026-05-15, never previously given a dedicated Sunday focus while Games got 09-13 and Lightfin got 09-06). Deep-read work/overview.md and work/source-workday-disruption-debate-2026.md in full: every substantive cross-domain link the debate supports (Mobley v. Workday discrimination suit, the ABN framework, Dwarkesh's Agent Civilizations incident, idea-wday.md's short-research gap) has already been made in prior runs, and no new Work material has arrived since May — so the domain itself yielded nothing new today. Instead, reconciling today's own Finance log entries surfaced a real pipeline-diagnosis error: finance/models/model-portfolio-management.md's strategy-feedback-loop review flags the Turso 'signals' table's Magic Formula rows as 10 days stale and asks whether the screening job has stopped firing — but log.md shows an mf-update job ran the same day with a Top 3 (MGNS/DNLM/GSK) identical to 2026-09-13's. Checking scheduled-task configs outside the wiki (portfolio-management-briefing/SKILL.md) explains why both are true: there are three separate, redundant Magic Formula computations (mf-update's own small-universe scrape, the full ~1,350-ticker Turso universe, and a third path in market-watchlist-tracker), and the SKILL.md already notes mf-update 'hasn't been retired... flagged separately for Mike to decide.' The small-universe job never stopped — it's the larger Turso-universe screen that's actually stalled, and nothing in the wiki records that these are different jobs. Concrete next step: add a note to model-portfolio-management.md naming the three-pipeline split so future stale-screen diagnoses point at the right job.
